lawyer:
Mohammad Habib Ahmed ------- For the petitioner.
Rafiqur Rahman ------- For opposite party.
parties:
Maram Ali ------- Petitioner.
Vs.
The State and ors ------- Respondents.
full_judgment: Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the O.Ps. contends before me that the paddy was seized not from the proceeding land but from a different piece of land belonging to O.P. Nos. 2 and 3. So the learned Magistrate rightly passed order for return of the seized paddy in favor of the O.P. Nos. 2 and 3. Moreover as the order dated 3-7-75 was an order under section 144 Cr.P.C. the order already lost its force on expiry of 60 days from the date of the order, as such the order is a dead order and it cannot be set aside. From the petition which was filed by O.P. Nos. 2 and 3 under section 144 Cr.P.C. it will appear that in the schedule of the petition they described the disputed land as 2 acres of land appertaining to Dag. No.5/12 of Khatian No. 2/12 of mouza Mirjargarh. The seizure list shows that the paddy of dag No. 5/42 of khatian No.1/12 of the same mouza was seized. Anyway, as the dispute was relating to land the learned Magistrate ought to have converted the case into a case under section 145 Cr.P.C. and, on production of evidence of the parties he ought to have decided on the point of possession. He ought not to have made a finding regarding possession in the impugned order under section 144 Cr.P.C. The impugned order undoubtedly has been passed without jurisdiction. Though the order is a dead order, it may be prejudicial to the petitioner regarding his claim of alleged possession, and, as such, it liable to be set aside. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman contends before me that unless an order is made regarding return of paddy the O.Ps. from whose land the paddy was seized will be prejudicial. Moreover he also contends that if the order dated 3-7-75 is set aside the order of attachment order passed in the case under section 144 Cr.P.C. will revive. However on examination of record I could not find any order of attachment. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman in this connection points out to me the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate dated 1-4-75 stating that the O/C will maintain status-quo of the land. This cannot be construed as an order of attachment. As the impugned order was passed by the learned Magistrate without having jurisdiction, it is liable to be set aside and the learned Magistrate will pass necessary order regarding disposal of the seized paddy.
